name: CoreSiteReality
intent: Live-site map command surface: a full app shell (CoreAppSidebar + CoreAppTopBar) with a single "Site Reality" sidebar entry, a full-width headline stat strip (connected / online / active / inactive / manhours), and a three-column body — an Insights Map panel of levels and toggleable layers, an intentionally empty map stage for a real engine to mount into, and a PushPanel context column carrying weather, manpower-by-shift and equipment.
when: Starting a live-site monitoring surface where a map is the primary object and panels frame it
A screen whose headline figures must stay visible above a full-bleed canvas
A map surface that needs collapsible layer controls on one side and ambient site context on the other
whenNot: A map with no surrounding operational context -> use the Map component directly
Side-by-side comparison of two map states -> use Map Compare Layout
A content page rendered inside an existing app shell -> use a content-only template

chooseOver.component: Assembling CoreAppSidebar + CoreAppTopBar + KPIBar + SectionPanel + PushPanel by hand
chooseOver.because: Site Reality owns the shell, the stat band and both flanking panels, so a map engine plugs straight into the empty stage.
Safety Manager organises a route by header tabs; Site Reality keeps one persistent canvas flanked by panels.

allowedPlacement: route-level live-site surface that owns the full window
forbiddenPlacement: inside a scrolling page container (the map stage needs a bounded height)

derivedFrom.source: CoreAppSidebar + CoreAppTopBar app shell (Safety Manager) + PushPanel context column (Workforce)
extracted: KPIBar headline band above a full-bleed canvas
SectionPanel levels/layers column flanking an empty map stage
docked PushPanel context column (weather / manpower / equipment)

lineage.confidence: unset — scaffold, no held-out eval yet
notes: map stage intentionally empty - a map engine (Map, Cesium, That Open) mounts there
composed entirely from existing @core/core-ui components; the file adds layout and fixture data only, no new UI primitive
